subQuestions.questionText: The components of a DNA molecule that provide the code for protein synthesis are the …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Nitrogenous bases form the genetic code of DNA. The specific sequence of bases (adenine, thymine, guanine, cytosine) provides the instructions for protein synthesis. Sugars and phosphates form the backbone; hydrogen bonds hold the two strands together.

subQuestions.questionText: During which stage of meiosis do spindle fibres begin to form?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Spindle fibres begin to form during Prophase. In Prophase I of meiosis the spindle apparatus starts forming as chromosomes condense and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

subQuestions.questionText: An individual has Down syndrome. In the karyotype there is an abnormal number of chromosomes at chromosome pair …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Down syndrome (trisomy 21) is caused by an extra chromosome at pair 21, resulting in three copies instead of two (2n + 1 = 47 chromosomes total).

subQuestions.questionText: An individual that has received an identical allele from each parent is described as being …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Homozygous describes an organism that has received the same allele from each parent (e.g. AA or aa). Heterozygous means different alleles; homologous refers to chromosome pairs; dominant refers to allele expression.

subQuestions.questionText: A plant species has a diploid chromosome number of 12. Which ONE of the following is the haploid chromosome number for this species?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
The haploid number is half the diploid number. Diploid = 12, so haploid = 12 ÷ 2 = 6. Haploid cells (gametes) are produced by meiosis.

subQuestions.questionText: Inheritance by multiple alleles in genetics refers to …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Multiple alleles means more than two alleles exist for a single gene (characteristic) in a population, though an individual organism can only carry two alleles at a time. ABO blood groups are a classic example (alleles I^A, I^B, i).

options.A: two alleles that influence two characteristics.
options.B: more than two alleles that influence one characteristic.
options.C: one allele that influences more than one characteristic.
options.D: more than two alleles that influence two characteristics.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following is a reproductive isolation mechanism?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Infertile offspring is a post-zygotic reproductive isolation mechanism — even if mating occurs between two populations, offspring cannot reproduce, preventing gene flow. Options A, C and D would promote interbreeding, not isolate populations.

options.A: Breeding at the same time of the year
options.C: Plant adaptation to the same pollinators

subQuestions.questionText: Normal human ova have …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Normal human ova are haploid cells produced by meiosis containing 22 autosomes and one sex chromosome, which is always an X chromosome. (Sperm cells can carry either X or Y.)

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following occurs in mitosis but NOT in meiosis?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
In mitosis, only two daughter cells are formed at the end of one division cycle. In meiosis, four haploid cells are produced through two division cycles. Crossing over, homologous chromosome pairing, and centriole formation all occur in meiosis.

options.A: Two cells are formed at the end of the division
options.C: Homologous chromosomes arrange at the equator
options.D: Centrioles form at the poles of the cell

subQuestions.questionText: The graph below shows the percentage similarity between human (Hu) DNA and the DNA of some species of African apes (Chimpanzee 98%, Gibbon 96%, Rhesus monkey 94%, Galago 72%). Which ONE of the following phylogenetic trees best represents the information in the graph?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
The graph shows Chimpanzee is most similar to humans (98%), then Gibbon (96%), Rhesus monkey (94%), and Galago is most distant (72%). The phylogenetic tree must show Hu and Ch branching most recently (closest relatives), while Ga branches earliest (most distant). Tree C correctly shows Ga branching first from the common ancestor, then Rm, then Gi groups with Hu and Ch as closest relatives.

options.A: Hu and Ch branch together with Gi; Rm branches separately; Ga is most distant
options.B: Hu and Ga branch together first; Rm and Gi next; Ch is most distant
options.C: Ga branches first (most distant); then Rm; then Gi; Hu and Ch are most closely related
options.D: Gi and Rm branch together; then Ch and Hu; with Ga branching separately

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: Division of the cytoplasm of a cell during meiosis
subQuestions.memoText:
Cytokinesis (1 mark)
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm that follows nuclear division (karyokinesis). It produces two separate daughter cells, each with its own nucleus.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The sugar molecule present in a nucleotide of RNA
subQuestions.memoText:
Ribose (1 mark)
Ribose is the pentose (5-carbon) sugar found in RNA nucleotides. DNA contains deoxyribose, which lacks one oxygen atom compared to ribose.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The position of a gene on a chromosome
subQuestions.memoText:
Locus (1 mark)
The locus (plural: loci) is the specific fixed position on a chromosome where a particular gene is located. Alleles of the same gene occupy the same locus on homologous chromosomes.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The process during which a DNA molecule makes an exact copy of itself
subQuestions.memoText:
(DNA) Replication (1 mark)
DNA replication is the process by which a DNA molecule is copied to produce two identical DNA molecules. It occurs during the S phase of interphase, before cell division.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: Undifferentiated cells that may be stimulated to develop into any type of body cell
subQuestions.memoText:
Stem cells (1 mark)
Stem cells are undifferentiated (unspecialised) cells that can divide and differentiate into various specialised cell types. They are found in embryos (embryonic stem cells) and in certain adult tissues.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: Mendel's principle which states that an organism possesses two factors which separate so that each gamete contains only one of these factors
subQuestions.memoText:
Segregation (1 mark)
Mendel's Law of Segregation states that during gamete formation the two alleles for each gene separate so that each gamete receives only one allele per gene.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The evolutionary theory that proposes long periods where species do not change, alternating with short periods where rapid changes occur
subQuestions.memoText:
Punctuated equilibrium (1 mark)
Punctuated equilibrium (proposed by Eldredge and Gould) suggests that species remain relatively unchanged for long periods (stasis), punctuated by short bursts of rapid evolutionary change.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: A tangled network of DNA and protein located within the nucleus
subQuestions.memoText:
Chromatin network (1 mark)
Chromatin is the complex of DNA and histone proteins found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. When the cell is not dividing, it exists as a tangled, loosely coiled network.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The natural shape of the DNA molecule
subQuestions.memoText:
Double helix (1 mark)
The DNA molecule naturally exists as a double helix — two polynucleotide strands wound around each other in a spiral shape, as described by Watson and Crick in 1953.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The phase in the cell cycle during which cell growth occurs
subQuestions.memoText:
Interphase (1 mark)
Interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle. It consists of G1 (cell growth), S (DNA replication), and G2 (preparation for division). Cell growth occurs primarily during G1.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the following statement applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
Statement: A group of similar organisms that occurs in a particular place at a particular time with the ability to interbreed.
A: Population  B: Species
subQuestions.memoText:
A only (2 marks)
A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same place at the same time that can interbreed. A species (B) is a broader concept — all organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring, regardless of location or time.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the following statement applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
Statement: The manipulation of biological processes to satisfy human needs.
A: Biogeography  B: Biotechnology
subQuestions.memoText:
B only (2 marks)
Biotechnology is the use and manipulation of living organisms or their biological processes to develop products and technologies for human benefit (e.g. genetic engineering, cloning). Biogeography (A) is the study of the geographic distribution of species.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the following statement applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
Statement: Discovered the structure of the DNA molecule.
A: Francis Crick  B: James Watson
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B (2 marks)
Francis Crick and James Watson jointly discovered and described the double helix structure of DNA in 1953, using X-ray diffraction data collected by Rosalind Franklin.

subQuestions.questionText: In tomato plants, tall stems (T) are dominant over short stems (t) and red fruit (R) is dominant over yellow fruit (r). A farmer crosses a homozygous tall, yellow tomato plant with a plant that is heterozygous for both characteristics. Name this type of genetic cross.
subQuestions.memoText:
Dihybrid cross (1 mark)
A dihybrid cross involves parents that differ in two characteristics, each controlled by genes at different loci.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the genotype of a homozygous tall, yellow tomato plant.
subQuestions.memoText:
TTrr (2 marks)
Homozygous tall = TT (two dominant T alleles). Yellow fruit is recessive, so homozygous recessive = rr. Combined genotype: TTrr.

subQuestions.questionText: List the genotypes of ALL the possible gametes for a plant that is heterozygous for both characteristics.
subQuestions.memoText:
TR, Tr, tR, tr (4 marks — mark first FOUR only)
A plant heterozygous for both characteristics has genotype TtRr. During meiosis, alleles segregate independently (Law of Independent Assortment) to produce four gamete types: TR, Tr, tR, and tr.

subQuestions.questionText: Haemophilia is a sex-linked recessive trait (X^h). The pedigree diagram shows the inheritance of haemophilia in a family. State what is represented by the squares on a pedigree diagram.
subQuestions.memoText:
Males (1 mark)
In pedigree diagrams: squares represent males, circles represent females. Filled/shaded shapes indicate affected individuals; open shapes are unaffected.

subQuestions.label: 1.5.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: State the number of generations represented in this pedigree diagram.
subQuestions.memoText:
3 / Three (1 mark)
Generation 1: P and Q. Generation 2: R, S, T and their partners. Generation 3: the offspring of S and T's families, including U.

subQuestions.label: 1.5.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: State the number of offspring of individuals P and Q.
subQuestions.memoText:
3 / Three (1 mark)
P and Q have three offspring in generation 2: R (daughter), S (son), and T (daughter).

subQuestions.label: 1.5.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the LETTERS only of females who have haemophilia.
subQuestions.memoText:
T and U (2 marks)
T is a filled circle in generation 2 (affected female). U is a filled circle in generation 3 (affected female). Females with haemophilia must be homozygous recessive (X^h X^h).

subQuestions.label: 1.5.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the genotype of individual R.
subQuestions.memoText:
X^H X^h (2 marks)
R is an unaffected female (open circle). Her father P is haemophilic (X^h Y) and must have passed X^h to all daughters. Since R is unaffected she must have received X^H from her mother Q. Therefore R's genotype is X^H X^h — she is a carrier.

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows one cell in a phase of meiosis. Identify the phase of meiosis shown.
subQuestions.memoText:
Metaphase II (1 mark)
Individual (unreplicated) chromosomes are aligned at the equator of a single cell, which is characteristic of Metaphase II. In Metaphase I, homologous pairs (bivalents) would align instead.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE observable reason for your answer to QUESTION 2.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Individual chromosomes line up at the equator of the cell. (2 marks — mark first ONE only)
In Metaphase II, single chromosomes (each still consisting of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere) align at the metaphase plate, unlike Metaphase I where homologous pairs align together.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify structure A in the diagram of the cell in meiosis.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cell membrane (1 mark)
Structure A points to the outer boundary of the cell — the cell membrane (plasma membrane), which encloses the cytoplasm and regulates movement of substances into and out of the cell.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify structure B in the diagram of the cell in meiosis.
subQuestions.memoText:
Spindle fibre (1 mark)
Structure B represents the spindle fibres — protein threads (tubulin microtubules) that attach to chromosomes at the centromere and pull them towards opposite poles during cell division.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the role of part B (spindle fibre) in the movement of chromosomes during meiosis.
subQuestions.memoText:
It contracts/shortens to pull the chromosomes/daughter chromosomes/chromatids to opposite poles of the cell. (2 marks)
Spindle fibres attach to the centromere of each chromosome. During anaphase, they shorten, exerting force that pulls the chromosomes (or chromatids in anaphase II) to opposite poles.

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a labelled diagram of structure C as it would appear in the final phase of this meiotic division. Show the correct shading.
subQuestions.memoText:
Structure C in the final phase of Meiosis / Telophase II (4 marks):
• Heading (1 mark): 'Structure C in the final phase of Meiosis / Telophase II'
• Correct drawing (1 mark): Unreplicated chromosome/chromatid/daughter chromosome drawn from structure C only
• Correct shading (1 mark): One chromosome unshaded AND one with a shaded tip (OR both unshaded)
• Labels (1 mark): Any 1 correct label (e.g. centromere, unreplicated chromosome / chromatid / daughter chromosome)

In Telophase II, sister chromatids have separated. Structure C should be drawn as a single unreplicated chromosome (one chromatid). Two such chromosomes at opposite poles — one unshaded, one with a shaded tip — reflect the shading shown in the original diagram.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.1 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents the process of protein synthesis in a cell. Name the process which occurs at W.
subQuestions.memoText:
Transcription (1 mark)
W occurs in the nucleus where the DNA double helix unwinds and one strand acts as a template for the synthesis of mRNA using free RNA nucleotides.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.1 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the process which occurs at Y.
subQuestions.memoText:
Translation (1 mark)
Y occurs at the ribosome in the cytoplasm. The mRNA code is read (translated) and used to assemble a chain of amino acids into a protein.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify Organelle X in the protein synthesis diagram.
subQuestions.memoText:
Nucleus (1 mark)
Organelle X is the nucleus — the membrane-bound organelle containing the DNA where transcription (process W) takes place.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify Molecule Z in the protein synthesis diagram.
subQuestions.memoText:
mRNA (1 mark)
Molecule Z is messenger RNA (mRNA). It is produced during transcription and carries the genetic code from the nucleus to the ribosome, where it is translated into a protein.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO locations of DNA in a cell, other than in the nucleus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Chloroplasts AND Mitochondria (2 marks — mark first TWO only)
Both chloroplasts (in plant cells) and mitochondria contain their own circular DNA. This supports the endosymbiotic theory of the origin of these organelles.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the process at W (transcription).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 7 of the following points (7 marks):
• The double helix DNA unwinds
• (The double-stranded DNA) unzips / weak hydrogen bonds break
• To form two separate strands
• One strand is used as a template
• To form mRNA
• Using free (RNA) nucleotides from the nucleoplasm
• The mRNA is complementary to the DNA (A-U, G-C base pairing)
• mRNA now has the coded message for protein synthesis

subQuestions.label: 2.2.5 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Using the tRNA anticodon table provided, name the DNA base triplet that codes for serine.
subQuestions.memoText:
TCG (1 mark)
The tRNA anticodon for serine is UCG. The complementary mRNA codon is AGC. The DNA template strand triplet complementary to AGC is TCG.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.5 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the first TWO amino acids coded for by molecule Z in the diagram (the molecule is read from left to right).
subQuestions.memoText:
Tyrosine, Valine (in this sequence) — mark first TWO only (2 marks)
mRNA (molecule Z) sequence: U A C G U A A G C C C U G U C C U U
First codon UAC → tRNA anticodon AUG → Tyrosine
Second codon GUA → tRNA anticodon CAU → Valine

subQuestions.questionText: What is the change in the sequence of nitrogenous bases in a DNA molecule called?
subQuestions.memoText:
Gene mutation (1 mark)
A gene mutation is any change in the nucleotide sequence of a DNA molecule. It may result in an altered or non-functional protein.

subQuestions.questionText: The codon CUU (last codon) on molecule Z changed to CCU. Explain the effect it would have on this particular protein molecule.
subQuestions.memoText:
• The anticodon will be GGA / not GAA (1 mark)
• The last amino acid would be proline instead of leucine (1 mark)
• Resulting in a different protein / no protein at all (1 mark)

CUU is read by tRNA anticodon GAA → leucine. After mutation to CCU, the new tRNA anticodon is GGA → proline. The final amino acid changes from leucine to proline, altering the protein's shape and potentially making it non-functional.

subQuestions.questionText: A family wanted to identify the biological father of a boy. Blood groups: Mother O, Boy B, Male 1 AB, Male 2 B. DNA profiles were also obtained. Explain why paternity of the boy could not be established using blood groups only.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Either male 1 or male 2 could be the father of the boy (1 mark)
• Since both males have the I^B allele — Male 1 is I^A I^B and Male 2 is I^B I^B or I^B i (1 mark)
• The mother's blood group is O and must have the genotype ii / homozygous recessive (1 mark)
• The boy would have inherited the recessive allele (i) from the mother (1 mark)
• And he would have the genotype I^B i (1 mark)

Both males carry I^B and could have fathered a son with blood type B (I^B i). Blood typing alone cannot distinguish between them.

subQuestions.questionText: Who is the biological father of the boy according to the DNA profiles?
subQuestions.memoText:
Male 2 (1 mark)
The boy's DNA bands that are not shared with the mother's profile match the bands of Male 2's profile, not Male 1's profile.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain your answer to QUESTION 2.3.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Four/some bands of the boy's DNA profile match with those of the mother's profile (1 mark)
• The remaining bands of the boy match with the bands of Male 2's DNA profile (1 mark)
• Fewer bands match with Male 1's DNA profile (1 mark)

A child inherits half their DNA bands from the mother and half from the biological father. The boy's bands not shared with the mother align with Male 2's bands, confirming Male 2 as the father.

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE other use of DNA profiling.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark — mark first ONE only):
• Tracing missing persons
• Identification of genetic disorders
• Establishing family relations
• Matching tissues for organ transplants
• Identifying dead persons / criminals / suspects

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows the inheritance of flower colour in snapdragon plants. Red × White produces Pink offspring. The alleles are red (R) and white (W). State the type of dominance shown by the snapdragon plants.
subQuestions.memoText:
Incomplete dominance (1 mark)
Incomplete dominance occurs when neither allele is completely dominant, producing an intermediate phenotype in heterozygous individuals. RR = red, WW = white, RW = pink.

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 2.4.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
• The pink flower colour is an intermediate phenotype / a blend of red and white (1 mark)
• Indicating that neither of the alleles is dominant (1 mark)

When RR (red) × WW (white), all F1 offspring are RW (pink) — a blend of the two parent colours, showing neither allele fully suppresses the other.

subQuestions.questionText: A gardener crossed two pink-flowered snapdragon plants. Use a genetic cross to show the ratio of the expected phenotypes in the offspring.
subQuestions.memoText:
1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White* is compulsory + any 5 other points (6 marks):

P1/P2 Phenotype: Pink × Pink
Genotype: RW × RW
Meiosis
Gametes: R, W × R, W
Fertilisation
F1/F2 Genotype: RR; RW; RW; WW
Phenotype: 1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White*

Punnett square:
     R    W
R | RR | RW |
W | RW | WW |

*The phenotype ratio 1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White is compulsory for full marks. P1 & F1 / Meiosis and fertilisation must also be labelled.

subQuestions.questionText: Diagrams A and B show the ventral (bottom) view of the skulls of two organisms with the foramen magnum labelled. Which diagram represents the skull of a bipedal organism?
subQuestions.memoText:
B (1 mark)
Diagram B shows the skull of the bipedal organism. In bipedal (upright-walking) organisms the foramen magnum is positioned centrally at the base of the skull, beneath the brain, which balances the head over the spine.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE visible reason for your answer to QUESTION 3.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
The foramen magnum is in a more forward position (2 marks — mark first ONE only)
In diagram B the foramen magnum is located at the centre/base of the skull. This allows the head to balance on the vertical spine, enabling bipedal locomotion. In diagram A (quadruped) the foramen magnum is positioned further back.

subQuestions.questionText: Tabulate TWO visible differences between the upper jaws in diagrams A and B that represent trends in human evolution.
subQuestions.memoText:
Table heading (1 mark) + any 2 correct differences (2 × 2 marks = 4 marks):

| A | B |
|---|---|
| Larger canines/teeth | Smaller canines/teeth |
| Jaws with teeth in a rectangular/U shape | Jaws with teeth on a gentle/round curve |
| More protruding jaw / prognathous | Less protruding jaw / non-prognathous |
| Diastema present | No diastema |

(Mark first TWO differences only)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the significance of the shape of the spine that is associated with the skull in diagram B.
subQuestions.memoText:
1* compulsory + any 1 (2 marks):
• The spine is S-shaped* (compulsory)
• To support upper body weight
• For shock absorption
• For flexibility

The S-shaped (sigmoid) curve of the human spine is an adaptation for bipedalism. It distributes the weight of the upper body evenly over the pelvis and legs, and absorbs shocks during walking and running.

subQuestions.questionText: The herbicide glyphosate was applied to weeds in maize fields from 2009 to 2016. The percentage of glyphosate-resistant weeds was recorded each year (2009: 10%, 2010: 20%, 2011: 32%, 2012: 42%, 2013: 53%, 2014: 58%, 2015: 65%, 2016: 65%). Describe the change in glyphosate resistance over the time of the investigation.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Glyphosate resistance increased (1 mark)
• From 2009 to 2015 (1 mark)
• And remained constant in 2016 (1 mark)

The percentage of glyphosate-resistant weeds rose steadily from 10% in 2009 to 65% in 2015, then plateaued at 65% in 2016.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage increase in glyphosate resistant weeds from 2010 to 2015. Show ALL your working.
subQuestions.memoText:
225% (3 marks)

Working:
(65 − 20) / 20 × 100
= 45/20 × 100
= 225%

Mark allocation:
• Correct values identified: 65% (2015) and 20% (2010) (1 mark)
• Correct formula applied (1 mark)
• Correct answer: 225% (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Scientists isolated the gene for glyphosate resistance from the weeds and used it to genetically modify the maize plants. Explain the economic benefit of making the maize plants resistant to glyphosate.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE complete chain of reasoning (3 marks):

Option 1:
• The glyphosate will not kill the maize (1 mark)
• A greater yield of maize (1 mark)
• Means greater profit (1 mark)

Option 2:
• Application of glyphosate does not have to be selective (1 mark)
• This will save on labour / time / costs (1 mark)
• Means greater profit (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a bar graph to illustrate the results of the investigation in the first four years (2009–2012).
subQuestions.memoText:
Bar graph criteria (6 marks):
• Correct type of graph (T): Bar graph drawn (1 mark)
• Caption (C): Both variables included in heading (1 mark)
• Axes labels (L): X-axis (Year) and Y-axis (Glyphosate resistant weeds %) correctly labelled with units (1 mark)
• Scale (S): Equal bar spacing on X-axis; correct numerical scale on Y-axis (1 mark)
• Plotting — 1 to 3 coordinates correct (1 mark)
• Plotting — all 4 coordinates correct: 2009=10%, 2010=20%, 2011=32%, 2012=42% (2 marks)

Caption example: 'Glyphosate resistance in weeds over 4 years / 2009 to 2012'

subQuestions.questionText: Lizards from Island A (insect-eating) were moved to Island B (fibrous plants, fewer insects). 36 years later scientists observed the lizards on Island B had larger jaws. Describe how the scientists could confirm that there was a change in jaw size between the lizards of Island A and the lizards of Island B.
subQuestions.memoText:
• They measured the jaw size of lizards on both islands (1 mark)
• And determined the average jaw size for each population (1 mark)
• They compared the difference between the two (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the larger jaws of the lizards on Island B would be structurally suited to eat tough fibrous leaves.
subQuestions.memoText:
• A larger jaw allows for better muscle attachment / more teeth / larger teeth (1 mark)
• Thereby increasing the bite force / ability (1 mark)
• To break down the fibrous plant material (1 mark)

Larger jaws provide greater leverage and stronger muscles, producing sufficient force to chew and process tough, fibrous leaves that smaller jaws could not break down effectively.

subQuestions.questionText: How did the scientists determine that the two populations of lizards on both islands still belong to the same species?
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• They allowed the lizards of the two islands to mate
• And determined that they were able to interbreed
• And give rise to fertile offspring

Two populations belong to the same species if they can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the possible effect that the evolution of the lizards has on biodiversity.
subQuestions.memoText:
Either answer is acceptable (2 marks):

Option 1:
• Biodiversity remains the same / there is no effect
• Because the number of species remains the same / a new species has not been formed

Option 2:
• Biodiversity decreases
• Because some species of plants eaten on Island B could become extinct (through over-predation by lizards with larger jaws)

subQuestions.questionText: Use Darwin's theory of natural selection to explain the evolution of lizards with larger jaws.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 7 of the following points (7 marks):
• There is variation in the size of the lizards' jaws
• Some have small jaws and others have large jaws
• Due to the larger supply of (fibrous) plants / fewer insects
• Those with smaller jaws will be unable to feed
• And die
• The lizards with the larger jaws will have more food
• And survive
• To reproduce
• The allele for larger jaws will be passed on to the offspring
• The next generation will have a higher proportion of lizards with larger jaws

subQuestions.questionText: State the 'Out of Africa' hypothesis.
subQuestions.memoText:
• (Modern) humans originated in Africa (1 mark)
• And then migrated to other continents (1 mark)

The 'Out of Africa' hypothesis proposes that Homo sapiens evolved in Africa and subsequently spread to populate the rest of the world, replacing existing archaic human populations.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the family to which modern humans belong.
subQuestions.memoText:
Hominidae (1 mark)
Modern humans (Homo sapiens) belong to the family Hominidae, which also includes great apes such as gorillas, chimpanzees, bonobos and orangutans.

subQuestions.questionText: What genetic evidence is used to support the 'Out of Africa' hypothesis?
subQuestions.memoText:
Mitochondrial DNA (1 mark)
Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is inherited exclusively through the maternal line. Comparative analysis of mtDNA across human populations shows that African populations have the greatest genetic diversity, indicating that humans have been in Africa the longest and that all modern humans share a common African ancestor.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how fossil evidence is used to support the 'Out of Africa' hypothesis.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4 of the following points (4 marks):
• Fossils of Ardipithecus were found in Africa only
• Fossils of Australopithecus were found in Africa only
• Fossils of Homo habilis were found in Africa only
• The oldest fossils of Homo erectus were found in Africa
• The oldest fossils of Homo sapiens were found in Africa

The fossil record consistently shows that the earliest specimens of each hominid genus/species are found in Africa, with progressively younger fossils found on other continents — consistent with migration out of Africa.
